summary: Retain consumed mailbox replay proofs across unchanged live-stream updates

replay.detail: Native mailbox streams retain a consumed replay proof across heartbeats, safety checks and durable wakes while its inputs stay unchanged. A new unresolved channel loss clears the proof. A change to the fence subject, component, incarnation or epoch, native peer, process birth, lease owner or native ownership sequence also clears it. A current admitted report can then prove the existing replay nonce again and recover the new loss.

schema.detail: Proof retention is connection-local memory. No schema migration, new durable record or fleet claim protocol change is required.

rules.detail: Report admission still checks current native process and provider custody, mailbox fencing and lease ownership for every report. Retained replay evidence never grants report authority or bypasses revocation.

compatibility.detail: Mailbox frames, replay nonces and delivery report fields are unchanged. Existing native clients continue using the same replay acknowledgement protocol.

downtime.detail: Deployment timings have not been qualified. Deploy through the normal fleet lifecycle; this change performs no live restart on another node.

manual.detail: No cache reset, mailbox rebind or manual replay acknowledgement is required. Reconnecting streams establish their own proof normally.

recovery.detail: A later channel-loss episode remains recoverable on the existing authenticated stream: its changed failure input invalidates the consumed proof and the next matching current ready report can append the existing fenced operational recovery claim. Retired epochs, replaced native peers and revoked provider custody cannot use the retained proof to recover a loss.
